clue.text: Did press find Ecstasy in psychedelic drug?

indicators.note: Ecstasy sits in the middle of the jumbled word
psychedelic suggests things swirled and distorted, so the letters of drug are rearranged

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A question about whether a pressing search turned up Ecstasy inside a hallucinogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'psychedelic' rearranges DRUG to URGD, and 'in' puts E inside it. 'Did press' must be read as a past-tense verb meaning pushed or insisted.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press them hard, so the past tense of one is a synonym for the other.

clue.text: Cosmic, like a little limerick apparently

definitions.meaning: relating to the whole of the cosmos, everywhere
split as UNI (one) plus VERSAL, a limerick being a single small verse

explanation.surface: A grand cosmic thought set beside the tiny, comic limerick.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful reading: the prefix UNI means one, so the word looks like 'one-verse-al', as a single short limerick is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cosmic applies across the whole universe, which is the core sense of the word.

clue.text: Army's joined with good spirit

parts.note: a host is an old word for an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: A regiment joining forces with the virtuous spirit of the times.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit of the dead seen by the living is a phantom, the same thing.

clue.text: Daughter stormed and ran away …

parts.note: it stormed means it poured, rained heavily

explanation.surface: A daughter flew into a rage and fled the house, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 4 Down, but the clues are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that drained flowed off and away, so ran away is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Tired of former partner and husband, a cast-off that gets time inside

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: gets ... inside says that a letter is taken into the middle of the cast-off word
inside, paired with gets, places the time abbreviation within

parts.note: a cast-off garment is second-hand, used

explanation.surface: Someone worn out by an ex and a husband, a cast-off now serving time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets time inside' puts T into USED to make USTED; the surface makes 'time inside' sound like a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted and tired are straightforward synonyms for being worn out.

clue.text: … is son covered in leaves?

indicators.note: covered in says the son letter is wrapped inside the departing word

parts.note: leaves as a verb, goes out, exits

explanation.surface: Continuing 3 Down: is the runaway son now buried under leaves?
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb meaning departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Is, as in 'there is', states being, exactly what the answer's verb asserts.

clue.text: Give a bit, being generous

parts.note: to hand something over is to give it
some means a portion, a bit of something

explanation.surface: Being generous means handing over a portion of what you have.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or gift is a generous, liberal one.

clue.text: Having run foolishly around bay, lay bare

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters enclose the bay
foolishly suggests the word run is handled carelessly and jumbled

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: Someone ran madly round a bay and stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' scrambles the first word to UNR; 'around' says it is split to wrap the small bay.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover something is to reveal it, to lay it bare.

clue.text: Instruments playing score for the listener with opinions

indicators.note: for the listener says the rugby word is taken as heard, giving its sound

parts.note: a try is a score in rugby
angles are points of view, slants or opinions

explanation.surface: Musicians playing a score for an audience full of opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY is a scoring move in rugby; heard, it sounds like TRI. 'playing' is a link word that belongs to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are percussion instruments struck with a metal beater.

clue.text: Party's full of students — they have very small houses

indicators.note: full of says the party word is filled with the students

parts.note: a do is a party; plural dos
L is a learner, so LL is two learners or students

explanation.surface: A student party crammed into tiny lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys of this kind live in doll's houses, miniature model homes.

clue.text: Soil dug up at No.1 turned over for quarantine

indicators.note: soil that is dug up is turned and broken, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned over says the number letters are read backwards

parts.note: No. is NO, and 1 is the Roman I

explanation.surface: A gardener digging soil and turning things over, in quarantine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug up' makes ISOL from SOIL; 'turned over' turns NOI to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is enforced separation of people, the state of being kept apart.

clue.text: Church suffering freeze

parts.note: suffering means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A congregation suffering in a freezing church.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze something and to make it very cold are synonyms.

clue.text: Eastern Times colour covers cold and obsolete

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

indicators.note: covers says the colour word encloses the cold letter

parts.note: a tint is a shade or colour
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A newspaper of the East whose colour section covers dead topics.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extinct no longer exists, so it is obsolete, out of use.

clue.text: Getting free small amount in the bank?

parts.note: saving someone is getting them free, rescuing them

explanation.surface: A modest sum freed up and deposited at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Money put by is kept in a bank account as one's nest egg.

clue.text: Capsized ship that's trapped way down in rushes

indicators.note: capsized says the whole assembly is turned upside down, read backwards
trapped says the depth word is caught between the ship letters

parts.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship
deep means a long way down

explanation.surface: A capsized vessel trapped far below among reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capsized' turns the whole ship-with-depth unit backwards, not just the ship. 'rushes' looks like reeds but is the verb meaning hurries.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush is to hurry, as a car speeds along.

clue.text: Meet where Cockneys buy chicken?

parts.note: a London accent drops the H, so a shop counter selling hens is heard without its first letter

explanation.surface: A Londoner arranging to meet at the poultry stall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech is the London working-class accent known for dropping initial H, so HEN becomes 'EN.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, and to encounter someone is to meet them.

clue.text: What goes up when it's coming down?

definitions.text: What goes up when it's coming down?

parts.words: What goes up when it's coming down?
parts.note: a rain shelter is put up when rain is coming down

explanation.surface: A riddle about something rising as something else falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol for rain is raised when it pours, the puzzle's coming down.

clue.text: Changing date to hold draw was trying

indicators.note: to hold says the shuffled letters grip the draw word inside them
changing says the letters of date are altered in order

parts.note: to tempt is to draw or lure someone in

explanation.surface: Rearranging a date to fit in a drawn match proved trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' is not a tied match here but the verb to lure; 'Changing' gives ATED, split open by 'to hold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempted is the past tense of attempt, meaning tried, so it matches was trying.

clue.text: Good person taken in by criminal with social worker's uniform

indicators.note: taken in by says the good person sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
an ant is a social insect and a worker
ST stands for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A saintly type duped by a crook dressed in a care worker's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant, a social insect, is the 'social worker' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant is unvarying, the same throughout, hence uniform.

clue.text: Something to soothe hosts about film's being shot here?

indicators.note: hosts says the soothing word holds the about abbreviation

parts.note: a lotion is a soothing cream
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A soothing cream hosting a film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests violence, but it is a film being shot on site.
explanation.definitionFit: A film made on location is shot in a real place rather than a studio.

clue.text: Fuss with rent over the top — one gets the wind up

indicators.note: over the top says, in a down light, that the torn word sits above the fuss word

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, torn
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Over-the-top fuss about rent, with someone getting nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: To get the wind up is to become scared; here it is read literally as a twister whipping the wind upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent spinning wind that whirls air up in a funnel.

clue.text: Fail to win in court in which one's real identity is hidden

definitions.text: in which one's real identity is hidden

indicators.note: in says the losing word goes inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: to lose is to fail to win

explanation.surface: Losing a court case in which someone's true identity stayed secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the closet means keeping one's sexuality secret, concealing one's true self.

clue.text: Hose may run up them, they run up hose

definitions.meaning: a fire hose is carried up the climbing frames firefighters use
runs in tights or stockings, which spread upward

explanation.surface: A neat reversal of hose climbing them and them climbing hose.
explanation.walkthrough: Hose is both a fire hose and old word for stockings, where a run is called a ladder in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both climbing frames with rungs and the runs in stockings.

clue.text: Get in boat at sea — and no bait prepared?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Climbing into a boat at sea without bait ready for fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: A second anagram also works: 'no bait' with 'prepared' as the signal gives the same letters, so the clue has two routes.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get hold of it, acquire it.

clue.text: What links 'Only Sixteen' and 'When I'm Sixty-Four', and who likes them?

definitions.text: What links 'Only Sixteen' and 'When I'm Sixty-Four'
definitions.meaning: sixteen and sixty-four are both numbers formed by multiplying a number by itself
fogeys, dull old-fashioned people, who would enjoy such dated songs

explanation.surface: A pop quiz question about two old songs and their fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Both are songs from the late 1950s and 1960s; 16 is four times four, 64 eight times eight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both perfect powers of two-times numbers and staid, uncool people.

clue.text: Quiet little gnome works to be ranked on this

definitions.text: works to be ranked on this

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
an elf is a little sprite like a gnome

explanation.surface: A quiet garden gnome being placed in a line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' are books, which stand in ranks along it.
explanation.definitionFit: Books are lined up in rows on a horizontal board fixed to the wall.

clue.text: Othello overthrown after plot in pillow-talk scene

indicators.note: after says the reversed piece comes behind the garden plot

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden

indicators.note: overthrown says the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Othello's downfall after a plot, fittingly in the bedchamber where he kills Desdemona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a garden plot, not a scheme; 'overthrown' reads Othello's epithet backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillow talk is intimate chat in bed, so its setting is where one sleeps.

clue.text: After work, time for something dramatic?

indicators.note: after says the time word follows the work word

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time for something exciting once the working day ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music.

clue.text: Run as one in crowd scene

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run given not off the bat, such as a bye or wide
a film or stage performer with a non-speaking crowd role

explanation.surface: Running as a crowd member in a film scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bat-and-ball game, runs not scored off the bat are called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bonus cricket run and a background actor in a crowd.

clue.text: A puzzle designed to throw out a shock

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths, so a puzzle is a maze

indicators.note: to throw out says one letter is removed from the intended word

parts.note: meant means intended, designed
the second a in the clue, taken as written, is the letter thrown out

explanation.surface: A puzzle built to deliver a nasty jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in the puzzle piece is the first a of the clue; the second a is the letter removed from the intended word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is the feeling of great surprise, the same as being shocked.

clue.text: Neglected quartet reportedly arrived one short of a team

indicators.note: reportedly says the number is taken as spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: a quartet is a group of four
got, as in got there, means arrived
a football or cricket team has eleven players, so one fewer is ten

explanation.surface: A neglected group of four turned up, one short of a full side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been overlooked or neglected.

clue.text: Bear in booth

definitions.meaning: to bear is to tolerate or put up with
a stall or kiosk at a fair or market

explanation.surface: A bear sitting in a booth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both tolerate, as in can't bear it, and a market stall.
